OSPS-AC-01.01_justification: GitHub enforces multi-factor authentication on the account that administers this repository (passkey or TOTP at each sign-in).
OSPS-AC-02.01_justification: Collaborators are added manually by the owner with an explicit role; tokens in use are fine-grained and scoped to this repository only.
OSPS-AC-03.01_justification: Branch protection on main requires a pull request with 2 approving reviews and required status checks (build, Analyze javascript-typescript, Analyze actions); the sole owner keeps an admin override, recorded in each merged PR.
OSPS-AC-03.02_justification: allow_deletions and allow_force_pushes are disabled on main, so removing it needs an explicit typed confirmation.
OSPS-AC-04.01_justification: The workflow token defaults to read-only and every workflow sets an explicit top-level permissions block.
OSPS-AC-04.02_justification: contents:write appears only on the job that pushes gh-pages and the job that creates releases; the rest are read-only, with id-token and attestations scoped to the jobs that need them.
OSPS-BR-01.01_justification: No pull_request_target and no event fields interpolated into shell; CodeQL analyses the workflow files and OpenSSF Dangerous-Workflow scores 10.
OSPS-BR-01.03_justification: Pull requests from forks run with no repository secrets and a read-only token; publishing and release jobs run only on main or on version tags.
OSPS-BR-01.04_justification: Merged changes must pass review and required checks; workflow inputs (release tag) are quoted and validated against the existing release.
OSPS-BR-02.01_justification: Semantic versions 0.1.0 through 0.1.4, unique on the registry; 0.1.1 to 0.1.4 are also tagged in git (0.1.0 predates the tagging habit).
OSPS-BR-02.02_justification: All assets are named night-city-ui-VERSION.tgz plus .cdx.json, .sigstore.json and .intoto.jsonl, and report their sha256 digests.
OSPS-BR-03.01_justification: Every official URI (npm registry, GitHub Pages site, repository, issue tracker) is HTTPS, and Pages has HTTPS enforcement enabled.
OSPS-BR-03.02_justification: TLS with certificate validation; npm additionally checks each tarball against its sha512 integrity value and the registry signature.
OSPS-BR-04.01_justification: CHANGELOG.md (Keep a Changelog) is maintained per version and now ships inside the tarball.
OSPS-BR-05.01_justification: npm with a committed package-lock.json, installed with npm ci in CI and at publish time.
OSPS-BR-06.01_justification: Each GitHub Release carries a Sigstore bundle and an in-toto statement; the tarball digest matches the npm artifact byte for byte.
OSPS-BR-07.01_justification: Secret scanning with push protection is enabled; the tree contains no credentials or .npmrc, and publishing uses OIDC so no npm token exists.
OSPS-BR-07.02_justification: SECURITY.md has a secrets and credentials policy covering storage, rotation, allow-listed install scripts and the leak response.
OSPS-DO-01.01_justification: Guide and Playground pages on the docs site plus the README quickstart and docs/COMPONENTS.md API reference.
OSPS-DO-02.01_justification: Issue templates for bugs and features, linked from the README; SECURITY.md covers the security-specific route.
OSPS-DO-03.01_justification: docs/VERIFYING_A_RELEASE.md walks through registry signature, sha512 integrity and the provenance attestation.
OSPS-DO-03.02_justification: The same guide shows how the attestation names the repository, workflow file, ref and commit that produced the artifact.
OSPS-DO-04.01_justification: SECURITY.md supported-versions table states 0.1.x is supported and only the latest release receives fixes.
OSPS-DO-05.01_justification: SECURITY.md states that superseded and unpublished versions are unsupported and affected ones are deprecated on npm.
OSPS-DO-06.01_justification: SECURITY.md documents the dependency and licence thresholds; CONTRIBUTING.md forbids new runtime dependencies; Dependabot opens grouped updates weekly.
OSPS-DO-07.01_justification: README Development and CONTRIBUTING list install, dev, test and both builds with the toolchain versions CI uses.
OSPS-GV-01.01_justification: CODEOWNERS names the account holding repository and release authority; SECURITY.md states releases are maintainer only.
OSPS-GV-01.02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md describes contributor, reviewer and maintainer duties, including who may bump versions.
OSPS-GV-02.01_justification: GitHub Issues and the pull request review threads are open to anyone.
OSPS-GV-03.01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains fork, branch, pull request, the protected main branch and who cuts releases.
OSPS-GV-03.02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md rules of the kit plus the pull request template checklist.
OSPS-GV-04.01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md: trust is earned through reviewed pull requests and permissions are granted manually at the lowest level.
OSPS-LE-01.01_justification: No per-commit legal assertion is enforced today (no DCO sign-off or ICA). Contributions are covered by GitHub Terms section D.6 and the CONTRIBUTING license notice; adding a sign-off check would close this.
OSPS-LE-02.01_justification: MIT, an OSI-approved license, in LICENSE and declared in package.json.
OSPS-LE-02.02_justification: Releases are the same MIT-licensed source; LICENSE is inside the published npm tarball.
OSPS-LE-03.01_justification: LICENSE file at the repository root.
OSPS-LE-03.02_justification: The npm tarball ships LICENSE and README next to dist/ (verified with npm pack --dry-run).
OSPS-QA-01.02_justification: Full commit history with author, date and diff is public, including every merged pull request.
OSPS-QA-02.01_justification: package.json declares no runtime dependencies (React is a peer); package-lock.json pins the development toolchain and is committed.
OSPS-QA-02.02_justification: No compiled or native assets are released (transpiled JS and CSS). A CycloneDX SBOM is attached to every release anyway.
OSPS-QA-03.01_justification: build, Analyze javascript-typescript and Analyze actions are required status checks on main.
OSPS-QA-04.01_justification: Single-repository project; there are no other codebases to list.
OSPS-QA-04.02_justification: Single-repository project, so there are no subprojects to hold to the same bar.
OSPS-QA-05.01_justification: Only source is tracked; dist/ and node_modules are git-ignored and built in CI.
OSPS-QA-05.02_justification: No binaries in the default branch. The generated gh-pages deployment branch holds build output only (site JS/CSS and latin woff2 webfonts from packages pinned in the lockfile).
OSPS-QA-06.01_justification: The required build check runs the Vitest suite on every pull request and before publishing.
OSPS-QA-06.02_justification: README and CONTRIBUTING run the suite with npm test; vitest.config.ts pins the jsdom environment and ci.yml (Node 22) plus publish-npm.yml (Node 24) run it automatically.
OSPS-QA-06.03_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires a new or updated test with every behavioural change, and the pull request template repeats it as a checklist item.
OSPS-QA-07.01_justification: main requires 2 approving reviews, but with a single maintainer who cannot approve their own work, merges currently happen through an admin override, so a non-author approval is not always enforced. A second maintainer or an organization with a bypass list would close this.
OSPS-SA-01.01_justification: docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md tabulates actors and actions: end user, developer, contributor, CI, registry, Sigstore.
OSPS-SA-02.01_justification: docs/COMPONENTS.md documents every export with its props, types, rendered element and ARIA behaviour.
OSPS-SA-03.01_justification: docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md records the assessment, with the grep evidence behind each claim.
OSPS-SA-03.02_justification: docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md analyses the attack surface (React-rendered text, URL-taking props, theme authoring, supply chain) and states what is out of scope.
OSPS-VM-01.01_justification: SECURITY.md is a coordinated disclosure policy with reporting route, timelines and version support.
OSPS-VM-02.01_justification: SECURITY.md names the maintainer and the private advisory route at /security/advisories/new.
OSPS-VM-03.01_justification: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled on the repository and linked from SECURITY.md.
OSPS-VM-04.01_justification: Advisories are published as GitHub Security Advisories and mirrored in the CHANGELOG Security section; none issued so far.
OSPS-VM-04.02_justification: There are no dependency findings that do not affect this project: the package has zero runtime dependencies.
OSPS-VM-05.01_justification: SECURITY.md defines the threshold: high or critical advisories on what consumers install block a release.
OSPS-VM-05.02_justification: The publish workflow fails before npm publish if the audit gate reports a violation.
OSPS-VM-05.03_justification: npm run audit:deps checks every locked package, development included, against OSV.dev on each change, with --self-test so a dead detector cannot pass.
OSPS-VM-06.01_justification: SECURITY.md states the SAST threshold: high or critical CodeQL findings on main are fixed before the next release.
OSPS-VM-06.02_justification: CodeQL (security-and-quality) runs on push, pull request and weekly, and its checks are required to merge into main.
